questions.q: What is Project 1's pool, as scoped in this lesson?
options: A simplified, teaching-grade AMM liquidity pool holding reserves of two ERC-20 tokens
A full production-grade multi-pool factory system
A lending protocol with collateralized loans
An NFT marketplace with escrow listings
questions.explain: The lesson scopes Project 1 as one simplified, teaching-grade AMM pool holding two ERC-20 token reserves — not a factory, a lender, or a marketplace.

questions.q: Which of the following is explicitly listed as OUT of scope for this project's pool?
options: A liquidity provider receiving a proportional claim on the pool
A constant-product swap function
A factory contract for deploying many pools
ERC-20 token reserves
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly excludes a factory for deploying many pools, a router, a protocol-fee switch, flash loans, and a third-party audit — the single pool, its reserves, LP shares, and swap function are all in scope.

questions.q: What testing approach does this lesson say will be used in Lesson 6, beyond plain unit tests?
options: No additional testing beyond manual clicking in a browser
Foundry-style fuzz and invariant tests
Only visual inspection of the Solidity source code
A third-party paid audit
questions.explain: The lesson states that testing will include Hardhat's unit test runner plus Foundry-style fuzz and invariant tests — the same testing concepts covered in this path's testing and DevOps material.

questions.q: Which network does this project's contract get deployed to, per this lesson?
options: Ethereum mainnet, using a wallet that holds real funds
The Sepolia testnet, never a wallet holding real funds
A private local-only network with no public access ever
No deployment happens in this project
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that deployment targets the Sepolia testnet and that the project should never use a wallet that holds real funds.

questions.q: Why does the recommended repository layout put the frontend in a separate folder from the contracts?
options: Because Hardhat forbids having a frontend in the same repository
To keep contracts and frontend as two clearly separated concerns, which a reviewer notices
Because React cannot run in the same folder as Solidity files
There is no stated reason in the lesson
questions.explain: The lesson frames the separate contracts/ and frontend/ folders as keeping two concerns clearly separated — an organizational choice a reviewer is likely to notice and appreciate, not a technical requirement of either tool.
